active.title: Organize a Pickup Match at Your Nearest Park
active.description: Find a patch of grass, bring a ball, show up. The World Cup puts soccer in the air everywhere this summer — you'll find players. This doesn't need to be organized in advance.
active.bonus: Play with at least one person you've never met before the game started.

active.title: Walk the MetLife Stadium Area on Match Day
active.description: No ticket required. On World Cup match days, the area around the stadium becomes its own event — flags from fifty countries, chants in every language, food trucks serving things you can't pronounce. Walk it.
active.bonus: Find someone who traveled internationally specifically for this tournament and have a real conversation with them.

active.title: 1v1 Penalty Shootout — Anyone Who'll Take You On
active.description: Find a goal — a park net, two cones, two backpacks — and challenge whoever's nearby to a five-kick shootout. The World Cup is decided this way. So can your afternoon.
active.bonus: Loser buys the winner a drink or a snack. No negotiating out of it.

active.title: Watch a Local Rec League Soccer Match From the Sideline
active.description: Every city has an amateur league running this summer. The skill level doesn't matter — in a World Cup summer, even watching a rec game at a public park has a different weight to it. Find one and actually watch.
active.bonus: Pick a team to root for before kickoff and stay committed to the result — no switching sides.

social.title: Watch a Group Stage Match at a Bar With Skin in the Game
social.description: Find a bar showing the match where the crowd actually cares — not the nearest sports bar, but the one in a neighborhood where people have family ties to a team on the field. The reaction is the show.
social.bonus: Sit next to someone wearing the jersey of the team you're not rooting for and have one real conversation before the final whistle.

social.title: Find a Jersey You Can't Identify and Ask About the Team
social.description: The World Cup puts 48 national jerseys on the streets. Find one you can't immediately place — not England, not Brazil — and ask the person wearing it about their country's team and why they're here.
social.bonus: Learn one fact about that team's World Cup history before the conversation ends.

social.title: Host a Watch Party With Food From a Competing Nation
social.description: Pick a match, pick one of the nations playing in it, cook or order food from that country. You don't have to care about either team — make the food the excuse and the match the backdrop.
social.bonus: Everyone at the party picks a team to support before kickoff. No changing sides at halftime.

social.title: Go to the FIFA Fan Festival
social.description: The official World Cup fan festival is where the tournament lives for everyone without a ticket — giant screens, national team activations, and a crowd that's traveled from everywhere just to be exactly there.
social.bonus: Stay for an entire match broadcast without leaving your spot. Full 90 minutes, one place.

chill.title: Watch a Full Match in a Language You Don't Speak
chill.description: Find the Spanish broadcast, the Portuguese feed, the Arabic stream — watch an entire match with commentary you can't understand and let the crowd noise, the visuals, and the tension carry you through it.
chill.bonus: Don't switch to the English broadcast at halftime. Full 90 minutes in the foreign feed.

chill.title: Find Somewhere to Watch a Knockout Match Outdoors
chill.description: A park screen, a plaza with a TV in the window, a bar with open doors spilling sound onto the street — find somewhere that isn't your couch for a knockout round. The World Cup is a communal event. Treat it like one.
chill.bonus: Don't look at your phone during the 90 minutes. Stoppage time counts.

chill.title: Watch the Entire Opening Match Start to Finish
chill.description: The opening match of the tournament is the one moment the whole planet watches the same thing at the same time. Find it, sit down, and give it your full attention — no multitasking, no second screen.
chill.bonus: Invite one person to watch it with you who wouldn't have watched it alone.

chill.title: Watch a Match With Someone Who Has Never Seen Soccer
chill.description: Explain the offside rule. Watch their face when someone scores. Answer every question, no matter how basic. This is the best version of the World Cup — seeing it fresh through someone who has no idea what they're watching yet.
chill.bonus: By the final whistle, they have to be able to explain the offside rule back to you. Correctly.

foodie.title: Eat at a Restaurant From a Competing Nation
foodie.description: 48 countries are playing in this World Cup. New York has a restaurant from almost all of them. Pick a team you like the look of and eat their food today — Senegalese, Moroccan, Ecuadorian, Moroccan, whatever draws you.
foodie.bonus: Order something you can't pronounce without asking the server how to say it first.

foodie.title: Food Crawl Through Jackson Heights, Queens
foodie.description: Jackson Heights is the most internationally diverse square mile in New York and the unofficial soccer capital of the city. During the World Cup it's another level entirely — walk Roosevelt Avenue and eat whatever draws you in.
foodie.bonus: Eat food from at least three different countries without planning which three in advance.

foodie.title: Order Food From a Country You've Never Tried
foodie.description: Not a country you're unfamiliar with — a country whose food you have genuinely never eaten. The World Cup has 48 of them to choose from. Pick one. This is the year to close the gap.
foodie.bonus: Don't research the dishes in advance. Order by description alone — ask the server what they'd eat.

foodie.title: Dinner After a Knockout Match in a Neighborhood With Skin in the Game
foodie.description: After a knockout result — especially a dramatic one — the restaurants in neighborhoods tied to the losing or winning country are electric with emotion. Find one, get a seat, and sit in the aftermath.
foodie.bonus: Sit near a table that's clearly celebrating or devastated and let the energy of their result set the mood for your whole meal.

adventure.title: Play FIFA on Console — Pick a World Cup Nation
adventure.description: During the tournament, the online lobby is full of people playing the exact teams competing in real life. Get on, pick a World Cup nation — not your default club, a national team — and see how it plays out.
adventure.bonus: Play as a country you know almost nothing about. Learn three real facts about their team before you start.

adventure.title: Score a Goal — Any Way You Can Find
adventure.description: Find a goal — a park net, a pickup game, two backpacks as posts — and put the ball in it. It doesn't have to be competitive or official. Just find a net and score in it.
adventure.bonus: Celebrate like you meant it. Full celebration — arms out, run, the whole thing. No self-consciousness.

adventure.title: Try Every Angle to Get a Ticket to a Match
adventure.description: The secondary market, a contact with a connection, a cancellation, standing outside the gate on the day — try every legitimate angle to get into a World Cup match. You might not succeed. The attempt is the activity.
adventure.bonus: If you get in, talk to the person sitting next to you for the entire first half. No phone.

adventure.title: Find the Neighborhood That's Celebrating After a Knockout
adventure.description: When a knockout match ends, whoever just won has people celebrating somewhere in New York — a neighborhood, a bar strip, a plaza. Figure out where and go there. You don't need to know in advance. The crowd tells you.
adventure.bonus: Stay in that neighborhood for at least two hours after you arrive. Don't leave when it peaks.
